# Baseline processing time

<!-- Generated by benchmarks/baselines/stonesoup/compare.py. Machine dependent: not byte-reproducible, unlike docs/evaluation-baseline.md. -->

Wall-clock processing time per run, on the runs of [evaluation-baseline.md](../evaluation-baseline.md). What is timed is the same for both: every measurement consumed scan by scan and the tracks extrapolated to every truth instant. Reading and decoding the files and scoring are not timed.

| | |
|---|---|
| CPU | Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 7 155H, 22 logical CPUs |
| OS | Linux 6.18.58.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 |
| Sifted | C++20, `release` preset (`-O3`, `-ffp-contract=off`), single thread, runs one after another (`sifted_montecarlo --timing`) |
| Stone Soup | 1.9.1, CPython 3.12.3, numpy 2.5.5, one thread per run (BLAS threads 1), 20 runs in parallel processes |

Limits of this comparison: the languages differ (compiled C++ against interpreted Python on numpy), Stone Soup is a general framework built for clarity and flexibility (objects per state, hypothesis and detection), and parallel processes share caches and memory bandwidth, which slows each a little. The ratio shows the order of magnitude, not a property of either algorithm.
